items.headline: Flood Warning issued August 12 at 11:12PM AKDT until August 14 at 4:30AM AKDT by NWS Juneau AK
items.description:
Mendenhall Lake gauge levels, along with USGS imagery from Suicide
Basin and water levels within the basin, indicate that the basin is
continuing its release of water into Mendenhall Lake and River.
Levels on the Mendenhall Lake and River will rise through tonight as
the release continues, with a forecast crest between 16.1 to 16.6
feet expected Thursday between 10am to 2pm.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by a glacier-dammed lake outburst continues.

* WHERE...The Mendenhall Lake And River near the M
items.instruction:
Stay tuned to further developments by listening to your local radio,
television, or NOAA Weather Radio for further information.

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the

items.headline: Heat Advisory issued August 12 at 9:44PM AKDT until August 14 at 7:00PM AKDT by NWS Juneau AK
items.description:
* WHAT...Temperatures in the lower 80s.

* WHERE...Haines Borough and Klukwan and Municipality of Skagway.

* WHEN...Until 7 PM AKDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...Individuals not accustomed to these unusually hot
temperatures for this region may experience heat related illnesses.
items.areas: Municipality of Skagway; Haines Borough and Klukwan
items.instruction:
Drink plenty of fluids, and check up on elderly and vulnerable
relatives and neighbors.

Close curtains during the daytime to reduce sun insulation into the
home and open windows at night to allow the home to cool off. Utilize
fans or community buildings with air conditioning.

items.headline: Special Weather Statement issued August 12 at 4:16PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
The warmest stretch of weather so far this summer is expected to
continue into the weekend. High temperatures warming into the
upper 70s or lower 80s each day with lows dipping into the 50s are
expected. Areas of wildfire smoke across the middle Tanana Valley
are already reducing air quality. Light winds are unlikely to
clear out the smoke.

Drinking plenty of fluids, avoiding strenuous outdoor activity,
and limiting exposure to smoke is recommended.

items.headline: Heat Advisory issued August 12 at 2:28PM AKDT until August 13 at 10:00PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
* WHAT...Hot temperatures as high as 80 degrees.

* WHERE...Central Arctic Plains and Western Arctic Plains.

* WHEN...From 1 PM to 10 PM AKDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Individuals not accustomed to these unusually hot
temperatures for this region may experience heat related illnesses.
items.areas: Western Arctic Plains; Central Arctic Plains
items.instruction:
Take extra precautions when working in the sun. Wear sunscreen and
lightweight, loose fitting clothing. Try to limit strenuous
activities to early morning or evening. Take action when you see
symptoms of heat exhaustion and heat stroke.
